title: Analog IC Design Engineer
summary: Designs the analog parts of a chip, such as amplifiers, voltage regulators, clock circuits and converters between analog signals and digital data, at the level of single transistors. Works in a chip team beside layout engineers, who draw the circuit on silicon, and verification and test engineers.
dailyDuties: Design and size transistor-level circuit blocks to a specification
Run Spectre or HSPICE simulations and check noise and stability
Sweep PVT corners and Monte Carlo runs before sign-off
Review layout with the layout engineer and rerun post-layout simulations
Write block specifications and present design reviews
Compare lab measurements on silicon with simulation results

skills.expectation: Design transistor-level blocks such as op-amps, comparators and bandgap references
Simulate circuits in Spectre or HSPICE for DC, AC, transient, noise and stability
Sign off blocks across PVT corners, mismatch and Monte Carlo runs
Own at least one block family: ADC or DAC design
Own at least one block family: PLL, VCO or clocking circuits
Own at least one block family: LDOs or on-chip power management
Run post-layout simulations on extracted netlists and fix parasitic effects
Write block specs and present design reviews to the chip team
Guide the layout engineer on matching, guard rings and floorplan
Write Verilog-A or real-number models for mixed-signal verification
Characterise silicon in the lab and debug against simulation
Automate simulation runs with Ocean, SKILL, Tcl or Perl scripts
Post-process simulation and lab data with scripts

groups.label: One analog block specialty (data converters, PLLs or power management)
